topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: The Problem of Speed (0:00-1:00)
sections.content: Recall average speed as (total distance / total time). Introduce the limitation: average speed misses the 'peaks and valleys' of a journey. Transition to the concept of 'How fast am I moving right at this exact moment?'
sections.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle: The cheetah's average speed over 10 seconds is 60mph, but its speedometer reads 75mph at the exact moment of the pounce.

sections.title: From Secant to Tangent (1:00-2:30)
sections.content: Visualize a position-time graph. Show a secant line connecting two points (A and B). Shrink the interval between A and B toward zero. As B approaches A, the secant line morphs into the tangent line at point A.
sections.example: Animation of a sliding point B on a curve y=x²; as the distance 'h' shrinks, the secant slope visually approaches the tangent slope.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative (2:30-4:00)
sections.content: Formalize the visual logic into the limit definition: f'(x) = lim (h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Explain the numerator as 'change in y' and denominator as 'change in x' (infinitesimal slice).
sections.example: Using a drone's altitude function h(t) = -16t² + 100 to find the exact velocity at t=2 seconds by solving the limit.

sections.title: Synthesis & The Big Picture (4:00-5:00)
sections.content: Summarize that the derivative represents the 'instantaneous slope' or 'rate of change.' It is the engine behind velocity, growth rates, and optimization in physics and economics.
sections.example: A 'Robot Factory' analogy: If the input is material, the derivative tells us exactly how fast the output (product) is being manufactured at any given millisecond.

storyboard.title: The Problem of Speed (0:00-1:00)
lecture_lines: Average speed is total distance over total time.
But averages hide speed at specific moments.
We need speed at an exact instant.
animations: Create a point P and Q on a curve. Color: #FFFFFF.
Draw secant line connecting P and Q. Color: #FF0000.
Move point Q closer to P along curve. Color: #00FF00.
Show secant line approaching tangent line slope. Color: #FF00FF.
Highlight the resulting limit as the derivative. Color: #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: From Secant to Tangent (1:00-2:30)
lecture_lines: Visualize two points on a position-time graph.
The secant line connects these two points.
As the points close in, the secant line shifts.
The interval between points shrinks towards zero.
The secant line becomes the instantaneous tangent.
animations: Initialize secant line passing through two points. Color: #FFFFFF.
Visualize change in distance divided by time. Color: #00FFFF.
Slowly bring two points together. Color: #FF9900.

storyboard.title: Defining the Derivative (2:30-4:00)
lecture_lines: We formalize this with the limit definition.
The derivative is the limit as h approaches zero.
Numerator shows the tiny change in y.
Denominator shows the tiny change in x.
This gives us the exact rate of change.
animations: Display the formal derivative limit formula. Color: #FFFFFF.
Highlight delta x approaching zero component. Color: #FF0000.
Show function f(x+h) shifting horizontally. Color: #00FF00.

storyboard.title: Synthesis & The Big Picture (4:00-5:00)
lecture_lines: It drives velocity, growth, and optimization.
It tells us change at any millisecond.
animations: Summarize relationship between secant and tangent. Color: #FFFFFF.
Display derivative as instantaneous rate of change. Color: #00FF00.
Connect speed concept back to geometry. Color: #FFFF00.
